gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-sunda: Hairline-free and stern, Capture It stands tall with strokes that never swell or thin. Noto Sans Sundanese does the quieter job, its open-mouthed e crossbars and low cap-to-lowercase step keeping the text plain sans and easy to settle into.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-sunuw: Tall, tight and nearly sealed. Capture It leads with that, while Noto Sans Sunuwar opens its curves to let daylight in, and a slightly generous size lets those short ascenders and open bowls breathe.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-sylot: Noto Sans Syloti Nagri brings short ascenders, a tall x-height and an a with a bowl that opens up. Capture It slams the door shut beside it, tight and towering.

gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-tagal: Bent tubing, stood up tall. Capture It's strongest quality is that bold, uniform stroke, while Noto Sans Tagalog fills each line with a dense middle zone and curves that keep generous gaps.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-tagba: Capture It runs a towering lowercase with openings squeezed nearly shut, built for punchy display lines. Noto Sans Tagbanwa stays open and clear underneath, so give it a comfortable size.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-tai-l: Capture It is tall, tight and sealed, with no thick-thin flicker anywhere. gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-tai-v: Stern and stacked high, Capture It looks urban and commanding with its sealed-up letters. Noto Sans Tai Viet pulls its terminals back from the curves, so a long read feels light and open.
